newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Timber firm Ta Fu ends debut higher.
newsitem.headline: Timber firm Ta Fu ends debut higher.

text.p: Shares of Taiwan-based timber products processor Ta Fu International Holdings Ltd ended their trading debut at HK$1.27 per share, up HK$0.26 or 25.74 percent from an issue price of HK$1.01.

"A surge in price was expected in view of its IPO (initial public offering) response," said a research manager at a local brokerage. "However, strong profit-taking interest on the first day of trading capped its upside."
Ta Fu shares moved in a range of HK$1.17 to HK$1.45 on volume of 144.93 million shares worth HK$184.21 million.

Ta Fu offered 168 million new shares, raising capital to fund outstanding equity contributions to seven existing joint venture companies and to achieve further integration of its timber operations. Its IPO was 148 times subscribed.
Ta Fu has 19 joint ventures in China, an associate company in Taiwan and a subsidiary in Brazil.
Analysts said they expected Ta Fu shares to consolidate in the short run after the selloff.
"Fundamentally speaking, its earnings outlook is positive due to strong underlying construction demand for its products in China and in the (Asia-Pacific) region," one analyst said.
